How much flood risk is here?

FEMA's National Risk Index rates Jefferson Parish's coastal flood risk Very High and inland flood risk Relatively High, from expected annual loss.

  • Coastal flood riskVery High
  • Coastal modeled annual loss (county)$10,799,982/yr (Very High, 88th national percentile)
  • Inland flood riskRelatively High
  • Inland modeled annual loss (county)$75,821,880/yr (Relatively High, 68th national percentile)

Modeled annual loss is FEMA's estimate for the whole county (all buildings), not any one home's expected loss or premium, and not a flood probability.

Source: FEMA OpenFEMA. Data effective NRI 2023 release; retrieved October 22, 2026. This product uses the Federal Emergency Management Agency's OpenFEMA API, but is not endorsed by FEMA.

Am I required to carry it?

About 55.7% of the NFIP policy units in this dataset for Jefferson Parish are in mapped high-risk (A/V) zones — not 55.7% of all buildings. In a Special Flood Hazard Area a federally backed mortgage legally requires flood insurance.

  • Zone AE48,193 policy units
  • Zone X38,177 policy units
  • Zone B595 policy units
  • Zone VE530 policy units
  • Zone A0116 policy units
  • Zone AO6 policy units
  • Zone AOB2 policy units
  • Zone A2 policy units
  • Other or unclassified zones6 policy units

Zone mix by policy units (summed policyCount). Federal rule: a lender must require flood insurance on a building in a Special Flood Hazard Area with a federally backed loan (42 U.S.C. §4012a). This is the mix of existing policies, not of all buildings, and does not establish any one property's obligation.

Source: FEMA OpenFEMA. Data effective July 31, 2026; retrieved October 22, 2026. This product uses the Federal Emergency Management Agency's OpenFEMA API, but is not endorsed by FEMA.

How much does it cost here?

Among existing single-family primary-residence NFIP policies in Jefferson Parish, the median annual cost is $1,172, with the middle half between $1,008 and $1,376 (62,806 policies). This is what current policyholders pay — a new policy on a different building can differ.

Each policy's annual cost (premium plus fees), single-family primary residences. The bar is the middle half (p25–p75); the orange line is FEMA's full-risk price.

Coverage in force: $19,521,724,000 of building and $5,777,950,000 of contents coverage across all Jefferson Parish policies.

Source: FEMA OpenFEMA. Data effective July 31, 2026; retrieved October 22, 2026. This product uses the Federal Emergency Management Agency's OpenFEMA API, but is not endorsed by FEMA.

How do current premiums compare with FEMA's full-risk price?

53.3% of 62,806 single-family policies pay less than FEMA's own full-risk price; the median full-risk premium is $1,589 versus the $1,172 actually charged.

  • Median charged now$1,172
  • Median full-risk price$1,589
  • Pay below full risk53.3% of 62,806

Years to the full-risk price: under the statutory cap, premiums for most primary residences rise at most 18% a year (HFIAA cap, FEMA Risk Rating 2.0). At that maximum rate a policy at today's median ($1,172) would take at least about 2 annual renewals to reach the median full-risk price ($1,589). This is the cap on how fast a bill can climb, not a forecast of any one policy; statutory surcharges and fees are outside the cap.

Source: FEMA OpenFEMA. Data effective July 31, 2026; retrieved October 22, 2026. This product uses the Federal Emergency Management Agency's OpenFEMA API, but is not endorsed by FEMA.

Can I pay less than the sticker price?

None of Jefferson Parish's 0 NFIP communities currently carries a Community Rating System discount; they participate in the NFIP without the extra CRS premium reduction.

CommunityCRS classHigh-risk discountOther-area discount

The Community Rating System cuts NFIP premiums for every eligible policy in a community that does extra flood work. The discount shown is the community's rate; what share of its policies currently receive it is not in this data. Confirm with your agent.

Source: FEMA OpenFEMA. Data effective Community Status Book; retrieved October 22, 2026. This product uses the Federal Emergency Management Agency's OpenFEMA API, but is not endorsed by FEMA.

What do floods actually pay out here?

Between 1978 and 2026, Jefferson Parish had 135,664 paid NFIP flood claims totalling $3,504,603,594.

Orange bars are the three costliest years: 2005 ($2,693,640,615), 1995 ($302,821,900), 2021 ($93,410,456). Net building + contents payments by year of loss. Claims are matched by the claims dataset's county code, which may not exactly match a policy's property county.

That is 135,664 paid claims since 1978 against 87,527 policies in force today — a cumulative tally spanning ~49 years over a present-day snapshot, not an annual claim rate or a flood probability.

Source: FEMA OpenFEMA. Data effective 1978–2026; retrieved October 22, 2026. This product uses the Federal Emergency Management Agency's OpenFEMA API, but is not endorsed by FEMA.

How common is flood insurance here?

Jefferson Parish has about 45.1 NFIP flood policies for every 100 homes (87,527 policy units vs 194,109 housing units).

  • NFIP policy units87,527
  • Housing units194,109
  • Policies per 100 homes45.1

A coverage-commonness proxy: policy units include some multi-unit and non-residential policies and exclude private flood insurance, so read it as how widespread NFIP coverage is here, not an exact share of households.

Source: FEMA OpenFEMA NFIP + U.S. Census ACS 5-year 2023 (B25001), retrieved October 22, 2026.

How often is this county a flood disaster?

Jefferson Parish has had 35 distinct federal flood, hurricane or tropical-storm disaster declarations. The most recent:

  • 2021 — Coastal Storm: Tropical Storm Nicholas
  • 2021 — Hurricane: Hurricane Ida
  • 2021 — Hurricane: Hurricane Zeta
  • 2020 — Hurricane: Tropical Storm Zeta
  • 2020 — Hurricane: Hurricane Delta

Distinct storms by calendar year (one storm's emergency and major-disaster declarations are counted once), not individual declaration records.

Source: FEMA OpenFEMA. Data effective declarations through 2026; retrieved October 22, 2026. This product uses the Federal Emergency Management Agency's OpenFEMA API, but is not endorsed by FEMA.

More data: FEMA disaster aid & reconciliation

Did the government pay homeowners after floods?

FEMA approved $0 in Individual & Households housing help to Jefferson Parish homeowners across 0 disasters, on 0 valid registrations.

FEMA Individual Assistance is disaster aid, usually capped and partial — separate from NFIP insurance and not a substitute for a policy.

Our counts are checked against FEMA's official figure and the API's own totals.

What this data cannot tell you

  • Your own premium — it depends on elevation, coverage and deductible. We show where existing policies fall.
  • Private (non-NFIP) flood insurance prices.
  • Your address's exact flood zone — use FEMA's Flood Map Service Center.
  • Why premiums are rising — we show the gap to full-risk, not the cause.
  • A year-over-year premium trend — the in-force snapshot holds only current-term policies, so a like-for-like multi-year index isn't possible from this data. A per-effective-year median is shown only where several years of policies exist.
